reason: This passage from 2 Kings 6:24-7:20 (the siege of Samaria) demonstrates the opposite of the stated claim. Despite Israel's desperation during the famine and Aramean siege, Yahweh fulfills Elisha's prophecy of deliverance and salvation. The king's initial doubt ('May Yahweh not save you?') is proven wrong when Yahweh miraculously saves the people through the Aramean camp's abandonment. The officer who doubts Yahweh's ability to provide food is struck down, while the prophecy is fulfilled exactly as spoken. The text shows Yahweh demonstrating active loyalty and intervention on behalf of Israel, delivering them from destruction. There is no mention whatsoever of Yahweh considering replacement of the people with another people.
